transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-05-14
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Evan Ortiz (Redwood SE); Mira Alvarez (CTO, Pinecrest Labs), Tom Becker (SRE), Samir Khan (Product), Lina Cho (Security)

Auto-generated summary (auto, may be rough):
Redwood + Pinecrest scoping for POC to validate capacity sizing and tail latency at peak bursts. Customer to provide 48h sample traffic and success criteria. Agree to run replay and a dedicated-capacity benchmark across p50/p95/p99 latencies. Discussed token distributions, concurrency, and KV/prefix cache expectations. Security questions: SOC2, KMS, VPC peering. Next steps and owners captured.

Topics: workload characterization; QPS and concurrency; token distribution (in/out); benchmark plan and replay; security & networking; timelines; success criteria and go/no-go

--- Transcript ---
[00:00:00] Jordan Lee: Alright, hey everyone, thanks for taking time. Jordan from Redwood, i'm the AE on this. Quick round robin? just to make sure we got roles.
[00:00:08] Mira Alvarez: Mira here, CTO. we're trying to scope a POC for our clinical summarization pipeline at Pinecrest. thx.
[00:00:12] Tom Becker: Tom, SRE. i'll likely own the replay and infra access bits.
[00:00:16] Samir Khan: Samir, product. mainly around latency targets and success metrics.
[00:00:19] Lina Cho: Lina, security/compliance. focused on data residency and key management.
[00:00:23] Priya Shah: Priya, solutions eng. i'll lead benchmark design and measurement.

[00:01:05] Jordan Lee: Great. Mira, can you paint the high-level workload shape? QPS, typical concurrency, what your longest and shortest prompts look like?
[00:01:15] Mira Alvarez: Sure. So typical background, we have a mix of interactive summarization and batch ingest. core user-facing summarizations are, say, 20 to 50 qps sustained during day, but we see bursts up to 400 QPS for short windows, like 3 to 7 minutes, when a campaign jobs release. concurrency per model - around 8 to 60 concurrent active contexts depending on the burst. average input tokens are small, 30 to 80 tokens, outputs are longer, usually 120 to 400 tokens for summary plus citations.
[00:02:00] Tom Becker: to add, the burst profile is spiky. our 95th percentile of arrival rate during campaigns is higher because many clients kick off parallel summarizations. overall daily volume is fine, but tail latency kills UX.
[00:02:22] Priya Shah: OK that's helpful. When you say tail latency, what's the target you're trying to hit for p95/p99?
[00:02:30] Samir Khan: Business wants p95 < 350ms and p99 < 700ms for the interactive flow. For batch jobs we're OK with 1.5s p95. but the interactive SLA is the blocking one.
[00:02:45] Jordan Lee: Got it. Our engineering question is whether you need hosted or dedicated. Dedicated gives you predictable GPU pools and lower variability on tail. Hosted can work if burst routing + fallback is acceptable. Any constraints?
[00:03:00] Mira Alvarez: Data residency is critical. Some records cannot leave our VPC. so private deployment is preferred, but we are open to hosted for an initial read-only benchmark if it's easier. also, we need SOC2 compliance, SSO via SAML, and our KMS for key material.
[00:03:22] Lina Cho: yep, and audit logs for token-level tracing for a 90-day window. encryption in transit and at rest is required.
[00:03:30] Priya Shah: Understood. For benchmarking, our typical approach is: 1) capture 48 hours of traffic, 2) anonymize prompts, 3) define sample distributions for replay (qps, concurrency, token length distribution), 4) run a staged replay in Redwood hosted and then in Dedicated/Private for apples-to-apples. We'll measure p50/p95/p99, token-per-second throughput, GPU utlization, and cost per 1k tokens.
[00:04:05] Tom Becker: what about KV cache or prefix caching? our summaries often reuse patient metadata that could be cached. will the benchmark reflect cache hit rates?
[00:04:15] Priya Shah: yes we can model cache hit rates. if you provide prefixes or grouping keys we can run scenarios: cold start, warm cache (50% hit), and hot cache (90% hit) to show delta on latency and cost.
[00:04:38] Mira Alvarez: Perfect. Also curious about quantization impacts. our outputs must not hallucinate; we can't accept quality regressions for cost savings.
[00:04:46] Evan Ortiz: For quantization we're typically suggesting a profile based on the model. we can include a baseline with FP16 and a quantized run (4-bit) and include evals on a held-out prompt set to verify quality isn't regressing beyond an agreed threshold.
[00:05:02] Samir Khan: what threshold would you propose? 1-2% drop in rouge or something equivalent?
[00:05:07] Priya Shah: We usually use a delta threshold of <2% for critical metrics, and have human-in-loop checks for spots that the automated metrics flag. we can agree specifics when we see your eval set.
[00:05:23] Jordan Lee: Let's capture success criteria explicitly. Mira, Samir — what will make this POC a go?
[00:05:30] Mira Alvarez: Two big items: 1) demonstration the interactive flow at customer-like burst profile with p95 < 350ms and p99 < 700ms for 95% of the simulated bursts; 2) no unacceptable quality regressions over our eval set — clinical fidelity is mandatory. If both, we'll greenlight a dedicated capacity contract.
[00:05:56] Samir Khan: and cost per 1M tokens under our threshold — we've modeled X dollars with our current infra team, we need Redwood numbers to compare.
[00:06:05] Jordan Lee: Noted. We'll provide cost-per-token estimates for hosted and for dedicated sizing.
[00:06:10] Priya Shah: On the replay itself, Tom, what's the format of your traces? timestamps, prompt id, session id, model requested, and response tokens?
[00:06:18] Tom Becker: We can give: timestamp, request payload (anonymized), response token counts, client id. we'll scrub PHI and replace patient names with placeholders. we'll put the data in an S3 bucket with temporary creds.
[00:06:31] Lina Cho: Security note — we need to ensure temporary creds and that Redwood's hosts don't store PHI. also, we'd like to see a binding NDA for the playback bucket access.
[00:06:42] Jordan Lee: We can do that. We'll share a minimal NDA addendum and our data handling playbook. For private deployments we can talk about in-region on-prem or VPC peering.
[00:06:54] Priya Shah: For the replay load generator, we'll make two templates: 1) synthetic open-loop that reproduces QPS and token distribution, 2) stateful replay that keeps session context and simulates KV cache hits. That will help measure KV cache delta.
[00:07:10] Mira Alvarez: Nice. For token distribution: typical input 30-80 tokens, outputs 120-400, but we also have a tail of long outputs up to 800 tokens for detailed reports maybe 1% of traffic. want to make sure those tails don't blow up latency.
[00:07:26] Priya Shah: We'll include a heavy-tail sample so p99 reflects those rare long outputs. if you have histogram or percentiles that would help (like 50/75/90/99 token counts).
[00:07:40] Tom Becker: I can export token histograms. expect p50 input 45, p75 62, p90 120, p99 520 maybe. outputs similar skew.
[00:07:54] Jordan Lee: Good. On concurrency mapping, do you rely on session affinity? like do many requests share the same KV key (so prefix caching helps) or are they broadly independent?
[00:08:04] Samir Khan: many do share patient metadata keys within a session cluster — in our peak the same patient can get 4-10 summarizations close together. so there is locality.
[00:08:13] Priya Shah: That helps - we can model namespace-level cache affinity.
[00:08:20] Evan Ortiz: A practical note: to size dedicated pools we want to know your acceptable queueing behavior. Do you prefer throttling or queuing when hitting capacity?
[00:08:29] Mira Alvarez: We'd rather have graceful degradation — route to a cheaper model or degrade non-critical features during peak. we don't want users to see errors.
[00:08:38] Jordan Lee: Redwood supports fallback policies — we can route low-priority batch tasks to lower-cost variants and keep interactive on the faster pool. We'll show that in the benchmark.
[00:08:47] Priya Shah: For benchmarks, we'll run three phases: warm-up (to populate caches), steady-state runs (sustained qps), and burst windows to emulate your 3-7 minute spikes. we'll collect GPU metrics: utlilzation, memory, token/sec, and latency histograms at per-route granularity.
[00:09:10] Tom Becker: can you show the raw traces and the telemetry for debugging? we want per-token breakdowns and traces if something regresses.
[00:09:17] Priya Shah: yes, we provide per-request trace ids and per-token timing deltas where possible. note some kernel-level op times can be noisy but we'll provide the best breakdown.
[00:09:30] Mira Alvarez: about timelines — we're aiming to decide on vendor within 6 weeks. POC should complete in 2 weeks once we hand off traces. is that realistic?
[00:09:40] Jordan Lee: Yes, realistic. Typical flow: 48h traces in, redact and prep (2-3 business days), benchmark in hosted (2 days), benchmark in dedicated/private (3-5 days) depending on infra provisioning. target end-to-end two weeks if infra access is quick.
[00:09:56] Samir Khan: provisioning for private might add time, yes. what's the fastest route if we want to avoid waiting on on-prem?
[00:10:04] Jordan Lee: Use hosted for initial bench; that gives quick turnaround. then we can run a dedicated/private test with a staging VPC or even a bring-your-own hardware flow if you want.
[00:10:14] Lina Cho: For hosted we need to ensure PHI isn't persisted. will Redwood provide a temporary ephemeral config for the test?
[00:10:22] Evan Ortiz: We can instruct the hosted team to run in a no-persistence mode and rotate keys. But for full PHI-safe testing we recommend private VPC peering so traffic never leaves your control plane.
[00:10:34] Tom Becker: what's the expected GPU count for, say, 200 QPS peaks with your model suggestions?
[00:10:41] Priya Shah: it depends on model family and sequence length. rough back-of-envelope: for a 70-token input + 250-token avg output, at 200 QPS sustained you'd likely need on the order of 6-8 high-memory GPUs (A100 or equivalent) with optimized batching. for bursts to 400 QPS you'd use autoscaling / burst lanes to ramp up. dedicated pools give more predictable tail. note: we will produce a precise sizing after we replay your traces.
[00:11:07] Samir Khan: cost? can you ballpark per 1M tokens on hosted vs dedicated?
[00:11:12] Jordan Lee: ballpark ranges: hosted is typically higher per token but faster to start — we'll give concrete numbers in the pricing sheet. dedicated becomes cost-effective at sustained volume. we'll include a break-even analysis.
[00:11:24] Priya Shah: For the quality checks, please share the eval prompts and acceptance criteria. we'll run both automated metrics and a small blind human eval sample.
[00:11:34] Mira Alvarez: we'll share a 200-sample eval set with labels indicating clinical correctness.
[00:11:38] Jordan Lee: Perfect. Any legal/procurement constraints we should know about up front?
[00:11:43] Lina Cho: standard MSA plus addendum for data handling. we have an internal vendor risk assessment that needs SOC2, ISO27001, and an SLA with uptime >= 99.9% for prod. for POC we're flexible but must see certs.
[00:11:58] Jordan Lee: We'll attach SOC2 report and the template SAML metadata and KMS integration doc in the follow-up.
[00:12:05] Priya Shah: Quick technical deep-dive question — how do you want us to model stateful sessions? keep context in a Redis-like store vs full KV cache in the model runtime?
[00:12:15] Tom Becker: we currently store session context in Redis and send the small context with each request but we'd like to explore runtime KV cache to reduce token re-encoding overhead.
[00:12:26] Priya Shah: We'll include both options in the benchmark: naive re-send of context vs runtime cache with hit rates. we'll report delta in tokens/sec and latency.
[00:12:38] Mira Alvarez: excellent. also, can we test fallback policies during overcommit? for example degrade ranking quality or shorten output length automatically?
[00:12:47] Evan Ortiz: yes, Redwood supports output length caps and model variant fallbacks; we'll script a policy to trim outputs for non-critical flows during bursts and measure user impact.
[00:12:58] Samir Khan: what about telemetry retention? we need at least 60 days of request traces for debugging during POC.
[00:13:05] Jordan Lee: We can extend retention for the POC; we'll note that as part of the support bundle.
[00:13:12] Priya Shah: Ok i'm going to summarize the actual benchmark plan items: 1) get 48h anonymized traces and histograms, 2) Redwood provides synthetic load generator templates, 3) run hosted benchmark (cold/warm/hot cache) with p50/p95/p99 and GPU metrics, 4) run dedicated/private benchmark, 5) run quantized vs baseline and quality evals, 6) deliver report and cost breakout. any missing?
[00:13:38] Mira Alvarez: add: include a scenario modeling a 1% tail of 800-token outputs and show mitigation strategies.
[00:13:44] Priya Shah: added.
[00:13:48] Jordan Lee: Great. Let's capture concrete deadlines. Tom, can you provide traces by 2028-05-16?
[00:13:56] Tom Becker: yes I'll aim for end of day 16th, putting them into an S3 bucket and i'll share a pre-signed link.
[00:14:03] Jordan Lee: Priya and Evan will prep benchmark plan by 2028-05-17. We'll kick off the hosted run on 2028-05-20 and share interim results within 48 hours.
[00:14:13] Priya Shah: We'll also include a model quality pass and include blind human eval results within the same report.
[00:14:20] Lina Cho: I'll need the SOC2 + network diagram and a data handling addendum before we provide the traces.
[00:14:26] Jordan Lee: We'll attach those in the follow-up email.
[00:14:30] Samir Khan: One more thing - we have early concerns about vendor lock-in. show us how easy it is to export model traces and configs.
[00:14:38] Evan Ortiz: We'll provide an exportable JSON with routing policies and model version pins; not magic, file-based export.
[00:14:45] Mira Alvarez: ok, thanks. is there anything else on blockers?
[00:14:49] Tom Becker: only the NDA and the security checklist. Once those land, i'll upload traces.
[00:14:55] Jordan Lee: Alright, recap of next steps: Jordan to send pricing and NDA & security docs; Priya/Evan to send bench plan; Tom to provide traces; Pinecrest to confirm eval set. We'll aim to have hosted bench results by 2028-05-22.
[00:15:19] Priya Shah: Quick note on metrics we'll report: request-level p50/p95/p99, per-token timing, GPU queue depth, batch sizes, and cost per 1M tokens. We'll include plots and a raw CSV for your telemetry folks.
[00:15:34] Mira Alvarez: sounds good.
[00:15:36] Jordan Lee: Any objections to inviting product infra to the kickoff (Tom, Mira?)
[00:15:40] Tom Becker: yes please, bring them.
[00:15:42] Samir Khan: we'll RSVP.
[00:15:45] Jordan Lee: Great. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with meeting notes and the checklist.

[00:15:55] (meeting ends)
